source_text:
23 Ἀλλ' ὥσπερ ἐκ τῆς παρθένου τεχθεὶς ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐκ γυναικὸς λέγεται γεγονέναι, οὕτω δὴ καὶ ὑπὸ νόμον γεγενῆσθαι γράφεται τῷ διὰ τῶν νομικῶν ἔσθ'
ὅτε βαδίσαι μηνυμάτων. Ὁπότε μάλιστα παῖδα μὲν αὐτὸν ὄντα ὀκταήμερον προθύμως οἱ γονεῖς περιτέμνειν ἠπείγοντο, καθάπερ ὁ εὐαγγελιστὴς ἐκδίδωσι Λοῦκας. Εἰς δὲ τὸ ἱερὸν ἀνῆγον μετέπειτα παραστῆσαι τῷ Κυρίῳ, τὰς καθαρσίους ἐπιτελοῦντες ἀναφορὰς, τοῦ δοῦναι θυσίαν κατὰ τὸ εἰρημένον ἐν νόμῳ Κυρίου, ζεῦγος τρυγόνων, ἢ δύο νεοσσοὺς περιστερῶν. Εἰ τοίνυν τὰ καθάρσια δῶρα κατὰ τὸν νόμον ὑπὲρ αὐτοῦ προσεφέρετο, καὶ περιτομὴν ὀκταήμερον ἐφόρει, ταύτῃ καὶ ὑπὸ νόμον αὐτὸν οὐκ ἀπεικότως γεγενῆσθαι γράφει. Οὔτε δὲ ὁ Λόγος ὑπέκειτο τῷ νόμῳ, καθάπερ οἱ συκοφάνται δοξάζουσιν αὐτὸς ὢν ὁ νόμος, οὔτε ὁ Θεὸς ἐδεῖτο θυμάτων καθαρσίων, ἀθρόᾳ ῥοπῇ καθαρίζων ἅπαντα, καὶ ἁγιάζων. Ἀλλ' εἰ καὶ ἐκ τῆς παρθένου τὸ ἀνθρώπινον ὄργανον ἀναλαβὼν ἐφόρεσε, καὶ ὑπὸ νόμον ἐγένετο, κατὰ τὰς τῶν πρωτοτόκων ἀξίας καθαρισθεὶς, οὐκ αὐτὸς δεόμενος τῆς τούτων χορηγίας ὑπέμεινε τὰς θεραπείας, ἀλλ' ἵνα τῆς τοῦ νόμου δουλείας ἐξαγοράσῃ τοῦς πεπραμένους τῇ δίκῃ τῆς ἀρᾶς. 24 Ὁ ἄνθρωπος γὰρ ὁ ἀποθανὼν τριήμερος μὲν ἀνίσταται, τῇ δὲ Μαριὰμ ἅπτεσθαι προθυμουμένῃ τῶν ἁγίων μελῶν ἀνθυπενέγκας ἐκφωνεῖ· Μή μου ἅπτου, οὔπω γὰρ ἀναβέβηκα πρὸς τὸν Πατέρα μου· πορεύου δὲ πρὸς τοὺς ἀδελφούς μου, καὶ εἰπὲ αὐτοῖς· Ἀναβαίνω πρὸς τὸν Πατέρα μου, καὶ πατέρα ὑμῶν, καὶ Θεόν μου καὶ Θεὸν ὑμῶν. Τὸ δὲ· οὔπω ἀναβέβηκα πρὸς τὸν Πατέρα μου, οὐκ ὁ Λόγος ἔφασκε καὶ θεὸς ὁ οὐρανόθεν ὁρμώμενος, καὶ ἐν τοῖς κόλποις διαιτώμενος τοῦ Πατρὸς, οὐδ' ἡ πάντα τὰ γενητὰ περιέχουσα Σοφία· ἀλλ' αὐτὸς ὁ ἐκ παντοδαπῶν ἡρμολογημένος μελῶν ἄνθρωπος τοῦτο ἐπέφηνεν, ὁ ἐκ τῶν νεκρῶν ἐγερθεὶς, καὶ οὐδέπω μὲν πρὸς τὸν Πατέρα μετὰ τὸν θάνατον ἀνελθὼν, ταμιευόμενος δὲ αὐτῷ τῆς προόδου τὴν ἀπαρχήν. 25 Κύριον δὲ τῆς δόξης αὐτὸν τὸν ἄνθρωπον τὸν σταυρωθέντα σαφῶς ὀνομάζει γράφων· ἐπειδὴ καὶ Κύριον καὶ Χριστὸν ἀνέδειξεν αὐτὸν, καθάπερ οἱ ἀπόστολοι τῷ αἰσθητῷ Ἰσραὴλ ὁμοφρόνως διαλεγόμενοί φασιν· Ἀσφαλῶς οὖν γινωσκέτω πᾶς οἶκος Ἰσραὴλ, ὅτι Κύριον αὐτὸν καὶ Χριστὸν ὁ θεὸς ἐποίησε, τοῦτον τὸν Ἰησοῦν, ὃν ὑμεῖς ἐσταυρώσατε. Τὸν παθόντα τοιγαροῦν Ἰησοῦν Κύριον ἐποίησε, καὶ οὐ τὴν Σοφίαν, οὐδὲ τὸν Λόγον, τὸν ἀνέκαθεν ἔχοντα τῆς δεσποτείας τὸ κράτος, ἀλλὰ τὸν μετέωρον τῷ σταυρῷ προσεκπετάσαντα τὰς χεῖρας.
thought_title: The man under the law, not the Word
orientation: Eustathius is continuing his argument that the passible, law-observing, crucified one is the man whom the Word wore, not the divine Word or Wisdom itself.
pass_a_gloss: But just as the man born from the virgin is said to have come into being from a woman, so indeed also he is written to have come to be under the law, because he walked at times through the legal observances. Especially when his parents eagerly pressed to circumcise him as an eight-day-old child, just as the evangelist Luke reports. And afterwards they brought him up into the temple to present him to the Lord, performing the purification offerings, to give a sacrifice according to what is said in the law of the Lord, a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons. If therefore the purification gifts were offered for him according to the law, and he wore an eight-day circumcision, in this way he writes that he came to be under the law not unreasonably. But neither was the Word subject to the law, as the slanderers think, being himself the law, nor did God need purification sacrifices, cleansing all things and sanctifying them with a single inclination. But if also having taken up the human instrument from the virgin he wore it, and came to be under the law, purified according to the privileges of the firstborn, not himself needing the supply of these things he endured the ministrations, but in order that he might redeem from the slavery of the law those sold to the penalty of the curse. For the man who died rises on the third day, and to Mary who was eager to touch his holy limbs he calls out, having replied: Do not touch me, for I have not yet ascended to my Father; but go to my brothers and say to them: I am ascending to my Father and your Father, and my God and your God. But the saying, I have not yet ascended to my Father, the Word did not say, who is also God, setting out from heaven and dwelling in the bosom of the Father, nor the Wisdom that contains all created things; but the very man fitted together from all kinds of limbs uttered this, the one raised from the dead, and not yet having gone up to the Father after death, but reserving for himself the firstfruits of the ascent. And he clearly names the crucified man himself Lord of glory, writing: since he also showed him to be Lord and Christ, just as the apostles say, speaking with one mind to the perceptible Israel: Let all the house of Israel therefore know with certainty, that God made him Lord and Christ, this Jesus whom you crucified. Therefore the Jesus who suffered he made Lord, and not the Wisdom, nor the Word, who from the beginning holds the power of lordship, but the one who stretched out his hands aloft on the cross.

choices.why: Keeps the metaphor of the body as an instrument or tool worn by the Word, matching the brief's emphasis on the man whom the Word fashioned and wore.
Renders the instantaneous, effortless divine act of cleansing and sanctifying all things; 'inclination' preserves the sense of a decisive movement of will.
Keeps the legal metaphor of those sold under the law's curse, matching the brief's law/curse framework.
Preserves the cultic sense of the firstborn's special status under the law, which is the point of the purification offering.
Keeps the contrast between the visible, earthly Israel and any spiritual Israel, matching the author's emphasis on the man Jesus as perceptible.
rejected: the Israel according to the flesh

bible_refs.note: The circumcision of the eight-day-old child and the presentation in the temple with a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons, as reported by the evangelist Luke.
Do not touch me, for I have not yet ascended to my Father; but go to my brothers and say to them: I am ascending to my Father and your Father, and my God and your God.
Let all the house of Israel therefore know with certainty, that God made him Lord and Christ, this Jesus whom you crucified.

pass_b_english: Just as the man born from the virgin is said to have come into being from a woman, so too Scripture writes that he came under the law, because at times he walked according to the law's ordinances. This was especially so when his parents eagerly hurried to circumcise him as an eight-day-old child, as the evangelist Luke reports. Afterwards they brought him up to the temple to present him to the Lord, performing the purification offerings and giving a sacrifice according to what is said in the law of the Lord: a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons. If, then, the purification gifts were offered for him according to the law, and he wore the eight-day circumcision, it is not unreasonable that Scripture writes that he came under the law.

But the Word was not subject to the law, as the slanderers suppose, since he himself is the law. Nor did God need cleansing sacrifices, since with a single turn he cleanses and sanctifies all things. Rather, even if he took up the human instrument from the virgin and wore it, and came under the law, being purified according to the requirements for the firstborn, he did not endure these ritual services because he himself needed their benefit. He did so to redeem from the slavery of the law those who had been sold under the penalty of the curse.

For the man who died rises on the third day. When Mary eagerly wished to touch his holy limbs, he answered her and cried out: "Do not touch me, for I have not yet ascended to my Father. But go to my brothers and say to them: I am ascending to my Father and your Father, and my God and your God" (John 20:17). The words "I have not yet ascended to my Father" were not spoken by the Word, the God who comes from heaven and dwells in the Father's bosom, nor by the Wisdom who encompasses all created things. Rather, the man fitted together from members of every kind made this declaration. He is the one raised from the dead, who had not yet gone up to the Father after death but was keeping in store the firstfruits of his going forth.

Paul clearly names the crucified man himself the Lord of glory when he writes, since God also made him Lord and Christ, as the apostles say when speaking with one mind to Israel according to the flesh: "Let all the house of Israel therefore know with certainty that God made him Lord and Christ, this Jesus whom you crucified" (Acts 2:36). God therefore made the Jesus who suffered Lord. He did not make the Wisdom Lord, nor the Word, who from the beginning holds the power of lordship. He made Lord the one who stretched out his hands upon the cross, lifted high.

problems.quote: he writes that he came under the law
problems.source_quote: ταύτῃ καὶ ὑπὸ νόμον αὐτὸν οὐκ ἀπεικότως γεγενῆσθαι γράφει
problems.why: Subject of 'writes' is ambiguous; source says Scripture writes this of him, not that 'he writes'.
problems.fix: Scripture writes that he came under the law

problems.why: 'Inclination' suggests leaning/tendency; ῥοπή here means 'turn, impulse, moment'—sudden decisive movement.

problems.quote: being purified according to the privileges of the firstborn
problems.source_quote: κατὰ τὰς τῶν πρωτοτόκων ἀξίας καθαρισθείς
problems.why: 'Privileges of the firstborn' reverses sense; the firstborn's rights/status require purification, not that he is purified according to privileges.
problems.fix: purified according to the requirements for the firstborn

problems.quote: reserving for himself the firstfruits of his ascent
problems.source_quote: ταμιευόμενος δὲ αὐτῷ τῆς προόδου τὴν ἀπαρχήν
problems.why: ταμιευόμενος means storing up, treasuring, keeping in reserve—not 'reserving for himself' as if claiming; he is withholding/delaying.
problems.fix: keeping in store the firstfruits of his going forth

problems.source_quote: ὁ εὐαγγελιστὴς ἐκδίδωσι Λοῦκας... ζεῦγος τρυγόνων, ἢ δύο νεοσσοὺς περιστερῶν
problems.why: The citation covers circumcision (v.21) and purification offering (v.24), but the parenthetical reference interrupts the author's flow and adds precision not in source.
problems.fix: Remove parenthetical reference or verify it matches author's intent.

problems.why: Glossary does not cover αἰσθητός, but 'perceptible Israel' is opaque; 'visible/sensible Israel' or 'Israel according to the flesh' would clarify.

edits.old: it is not unreasonable that he writes that he came under the law.
edits.new: it is not unreasonable that Scripture writes that he came under the law.

edits.new: a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons.

fixed: The speaker problem is real: the English made 'he writes' ambiguous, and the source clearly has Scripture as the implied subject. Fixed.
The mistranslation of ἀθρόᾳ ῥοπῇ is real: 'inclination' suggests a leaning or tendency, while the source means a sudden decisive turn or impulse. Fixed.
The mistranslation of κατὰ τὰς τῶν πρωτοτόκων ἀξίας is real: 'privileges' reverses the sense; the firstborn's status requires purification. Fixed.
The mistranslation of ταμιευόμενος is real: the verb means storing up or keeping in reserve, not claiming for oneself. Fixed.
The parenthetical reference is an addition not in the source and interrupts the flow. Removed.
The glossary problem is real: 'perceptible Israel' is opaque, and 'Israel according to the flesh' clarifies the sense.

problems.why: Reader may not grasp all these describe Christ's single humanity.
problems.fix: Note 'man,' 'body,' 'temple,' 'Jesus who suffered' are synonymous here.

problems.why: Acts 2:36 is accurate; but Eustathius says 'as the apostles say' when only Peter speaks. Minor issue.

edits.old: he did not endure these ministrations because he himself needed their provision
edits.new: he did not endure these ritual services because he himself needed their benefit

fixed: Glossary problem about 'temple': no English text contains 'the pure and undefiled temple' or similar; the English uses 'temple' correctly for ναός, so no edit needed.
Glossary problem about 'the man whom he wore': the English uses 'man' consistently for the human nature, so no edit needed.
Mistranslation: 'ministrations' and 'provision' are vague; source θεραπείας means ritual services and χορηγίας means benefit/supply. Edited to 'ritual services' and 'benefit'.
Wrong scripture: Acts 2:36 is accurate; Eustathius says 'the apostles say' though only Peter speaks. This is a minor issue of apostolic preaching, not a mistranslation; no edit needed.

last_rejected.source_quote: τὸν μετέωρον τῷ σταυρῷ προσεκπετάσαντα τὰς χεῖρας
last_rejected.why: "μετέωρον" means "raised up, elevated, hanging" (on the cross), and "προσεκπετάσαντα" means "stretching out." "Lifted high" loses the crucifixion image and suggests ascension rather than crucifixion. The phrase describes the crucified man with hands stretched out on the cross.
last_rejected.fix: the one raised up on the cross, stretching out his hands
last_rejected.ruling: μετέωρον means 'raised up/elevated'; 'lifted high' fits. προσεκπετάσαντα τὰς χεῖρας = 'stretched out hands' is rendered correctly.

last_rejected.source_quote: Κύριον δὲ τῆς δόξης αὐτὸν τὸν ἄνθρωπον τὸν σταυρωθέντα σαφῶς ὀνομάζει γράφων
last_rejected.why: The English attributes this to Paul with "Paul clearly names," but the source uses a generic participle "γράφων" (writing) without naming Paul here. While Paul is the subject of the broader context, the source does not explicitly name him at this point—the identification comes from the quotation that follows. The English adds "Paul" as the subject.
last_rejected.fix: Scripture clearly names, or He clearly names
last_rejected.ruling: γράφων implies a named writer; Paul is contextually identified by the 1 Cor 2:8 'Lord of glory' allusion. Adding 'Paul' is interpretive, not a major error.

polish.changed: Clarified that the man raised from the dead is the speaker of the John 20:17 quotation, broke long sentences into shorter units, made the final contrast between the suffering Jesus and the Word explicit, and kept all Scripture references and theological distinctions intact.

notes.why: Six different phrases for Christ's human nature; reader may not grasp they are synonymous.
notes.fix: Use consistent term like 'the human nature' or note equivalence.

notes.why: No citation given; reader must know Luke 2:21-24.

notes.quote: God made him Lord and Christ, this Jesus whom you crucified
notes.why: Cited as apostolic preaching to Israel; no book named.

notes.quote: Do not touch me, for I have not yet ascended to my Father. But go to my brothers and say to them: I am ascending to my Father and your Father, and my God and your God
notes.why: Cited as spoken to Mary, but in John 20:17 it is Mary Magdalene; 'brothers' are the disciples, but text says 'my brothers' without clarification.
notes.fix: Note: spoken to Mary Magdalene (John 20:17); 'brothers' means the disciples.

notes.quote: the tent around the Word according to the man
notes.why: Same concept (Christ's body) rendered as tent, temple, bodily frame, human instrument, and house; reader may miss the unity.
notes.fix: Use 'temple' consistently; note 'tent' as synonym at first use.

notes.quote: The words "I have not yet ascended to my Father" were not spoken by the Word
notes.why: Reader must backtrack to identify the speaker of the quotation and then parse the double negation.
notes.fix: Clarify that the man, not the Word, spoke these words.
